info.name: MedAppoint - Reschedule Flow
info.description:
API tests for the user story: "As a patient, I want to reschedule an existing appointment to another available time slot, without having to cancel and book from scratch"

**How to run:** set `api_base_url`, `app_email` and `app_password` in the environment and run the whole collection in order. Nothing else is needed

**Authentication** is automatic. A collection level script logs in, caches the token and only logs in again when it is about to expire (the login endpoint has a rate limit)

**Test data** is created by the collection itself (doctor, date and time are picked at random from the API) and deleted at the end in `99 - Cleanup`

**Every request** also checks that there is no server error (5xx). Every `Edge - ` request also reads the appointment again to check it did not change

**Not covered here, with more time:** year 0001, February 30, a slot that already passed today, a slot outside the doctor hours, a slot with only spaces, SQL injection text in the slot, malformed JSON and an id bigger than the database allows. They were tried by hand during exploration and the results are in `docs/exploratory-findings.md`

**Failing tests are expected.** Each failing test is a bug found in the API, for example the reschedule response returns the old data, past dates and invalid time slots are accepted, and a taken slot can be booked again. See `docs/Functional-Testing-Report-Reschedule.pdf`
